chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a group of people who prayed in congregation while they were naked. He said: 'The Imam advances with his knees, and prays with them sitting, while he himself is sitting.'
ai.seo_question: How should the Imam lead the prayer if the congregation is naked or nearly naked?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith details the specific posture of the Imam—advancing on his knees while seated—to lead a congregation whose bodies are exposed, thereby preserving the validity of their prayer without requiring full clothing. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of *rukūʿ* (bowing) being performed by lowering the upper body while seated, rather than the standing bowing seen in other schools, ensuring modesty and focus during the ritual.
